subject: Urgent: sustained latency + 5xx on reserved pool — exec intervention requested
messages:
From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@heliospay.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai
Cc: Alex Ramos <alex.ramos@heliospay.com>, support@heliospay.com
Date: Sat, 27 Mar 2027 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production latency + 5xx spikes on reserved pool

Markus —

We are seeing a sustained increase in 95th/99th latency starting ~07:20 PT and a growing 5xx rate on our reserved capacity (pool rsv-hel-02). Traffic profile is unchanged; this started without any deployment on our side.

Current impact:
- 95p generation latency up from ~120ms to ~650ms
- 5xx rate jumped to ~2.7% (previously <0.1%)
- Token throughput for our reserved plan has dropped ~35% vs expected SLA throughput

We have a customer-facing payment flow that is timing out. Support attached logs and a screenshot of the Redwood console SLA dashboard (sla_dashboard_helios.png). Please advise immediate mitigation and whether you can commit capacity or fallback model variants.

—Sanjay
Sanjay Patel
Head of Platform — HeliosPay
sanjay.patel@heliospay.com

From: markus_klein@redwood.ai
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@heliospay.com>
Cc: olga_petrov@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 27 Mar 2027 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production latency + 5xx spikes on reserved pool

Sanjay — thanks for the data and the dashboard screenshot. We see the same signal in our telemetry. I’m opening an incident bridge now. Immediate next steps:

1) I’ve requested a temporary burst allocation from Dedicated Ops to cover rsv-hel-02 capacity for the next 2 hours.
2) Ops will attempt an automatic routing fallback to the compatible quantized variant (rwd-q8-opti) to reduce per-token latency.
3) We’ll rotate a rolling restart of the affected hosts to clear any KV-cache buildup only if it’s safe for your live window (I’ll confirm with Ops).

I’ll keep you updated on the bridge. Attaching logs snapshot you sent for the bridge (logs_snapshot_0327.zip).

—Markus
Markus Klein
Account Lead, Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.ai

From: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 27 Mar 2027 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production latency + 5xx spikes on reserved pool

Markus / Monica — quick internal status and recommended containment:

- Observed cause signal: KV-cache pressure + elevated GC cycles on g4-rsv-03; scheduling shows long tail on scheduler queuing. Not an application change.
- Containment we can do immediately (ordered by risk):
  * Route Helios traffic to warm standby pool (rsv-hel-warm) — low risk, adds ~80ms, preserves requests.
  * Enable model-variant fallback to rwd-q8-opti for non-critical endpoints — reduces resource pressure but requires validation for quality-sensitive calls.
  * Short rolling drain of affected GPUs with state preservation (may cause transient errors during drain).
- Ops has provisioned an extra 4x cards in us-west-2 for 90 minutes (temporary burst) pending exec approval to extend.

I recommend we route Helios to warm standby + fallback to q8-opti for background inference immediately, and hold rolling restarts until Helios confirms a safe maintenance window. If the warm standby can't be kept long, we should approve extending burst capacity for +8 hours.

Olga
Olga Petrov
Sr. SRE — Redwood Inference

From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@heliospay.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai
Cc: Alex Ramos <alex.ramos@heliospay.com>, support@heliospay.com
Date: Sat, 27 Mar 2027 13:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production latency + 5xx spikes on reserved pool

Markus / Olga — thank you for the quick triage. We have a hard customer SLA window at 14:00 PT and can’t accept elevated latencies in that window. Two asks:

1) Can Redwood commit to the warm-standby route immediately (we’ll accept the +80ms) and confirm this will be sticky for at least the next 2 hours?
2) If burst capacity is required beyond 90 minutes, we need exec confirmation of authorization and any billing/credit implications before we present to our stakeholders.

I’m escalating this to our COO (Cc’ing) if we don’t have a firm plan by 13:50 PT. Please confirm.

—Sanjay

From: markus_klein@redwood.ai
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, olga_petrov@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: sanjay.patel@heliospay.com, alex.ramos@heliospay.com, support@heliospay.com
Date: Sat, 27 Mar 2027 15:52:00 -07:00
Subject: Action required: exec sign-off for extended burst + temporary credits

Team — Helios escalation completed the bridge; warm-standby routing is live and holding the window but throughput is still ~20% under expected. Helios will need guaranteed capacity for at least the next 8 hours to satisfy downstream SLAs. Customer is asking for:

- Immediate confirmation that we will extend burst from 90 minutes -> 8 hours (extra 4x cards provisioned).
- A short-term credit to offset impact for today’s SLA miss and to avoid escalation with their COO.

Requested quick decisions for execs:
- Approve extended burst (cost estimate ~USD 6,800 for 8 hours) — approval needed now to keep Helios traffic stable.
- Approve one-time credit (recommendation: 30% of today’s invoice) as a retention gesture if we can’t guarantee throughput recovery within 8 hours.

If we cannot commit to the extended burst and credit now, Helios will request a contract remediation call with their COO tomorrow morning — high churn risk.

Proposed message to Helios (for approval):
"Markus / Sanjay — we have routed you to a warm standby and provisioned temporary burst capacity. With exec approval we will extend the burst for 8 hours and issue a one-time credit of 30% for today’s impacted bill. We will continue to monitor and provide a detailed RCA within 48 hours."

Please reply-all with a single-line approve/decline and I’ll take to finance/ops for immediate fulfillment.

—Markus Klein
Account Lead, Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.ai
